slides.texte_overlay:
unspoken rules of people who
seem effortlessly smart

they read every day

they read something real every day, even just ten pages. a daily habit of reading is the quiet engine behind almost every sharp mind you have ever met.

they think before speaking

they pause to think before answering hard questions. a short pause leads to a clearer answer, and clear answers always sound smarter than rushed ones.

they stay curious

they ask questions about everything, from how bridges stand up to why people believe things. curiosity is a habit, and it grows stronger the more you use it.

they learn in small doses

they spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in something new: philosophy, astronomy, art. effortless intelligence is really just consistent learning nobody sees.

they admit mistakes

they say i got that wrong without fuss. owning mistakes quickly is what lets them learn faster than people who are far too proud to ever admit them out loud.
